evidence.quote: Integrating continuous single-cell gene expression profiles with discrete-token large language models (LLMs) remains an open challenge: text-based methods are token-inefficient and discard quantitative precision, continuous embeddings preclude autoregressive generation, and single-codebook vector quantization cannot stratify biological scales.

representation_rationale.summary: RVQ is chosen to preserve quantitative expression information better than text serialization.

evidence.quote: RVQ-Alpha addresses all three requirements with a residual-quantized tokenizer whose codes are embedded directly into the vocabulary of the LLM as a fixed representation of 10 tokens per cell.

representation_rationale.summary: The fixed 10-token representation is intended to reduce the per-cell context footprint.

evidence.quote: Athird constraint compounds the first two: cell tokens must enter the LLM through its native token embedding table rather than through a separately learned cross-modal adapter, which would relegate gene expression to a secondary modality and add a trainable bottleneck between cell identity and the reasoning path.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors favor native vocabulary integration to avoid a separate cross-modal adapter and its trainable bottleneck.

evidence.quote: We develop scCoT-Synth , an evidence-grounded supervision engine that overcomes the coldstart problem of newly added biological tokens without requiring a cross-modal projector.

representation_rationale.summary: Evidence-first supervision uses the language-model objective to ground new biological tokens without a projection network.

evidence.quote: Compressing ∼ 20,000 gene dimensions into 8 discrete tokens inherently discards fine-grained expression information. Although this representation is sufficient for cell type classification, the loss of information may degrade performance on tasks that require precise quantitative expression values (e.g., differential expression fold-change prediction).

representation_rationale.summary: The authors acknowledge information loss for tasks requiring precise quantitative expression values.

A conclusion-blind elicitation protocol prevents the teacher from short-circuiting this process.
